name: Hornspace Knit Beanie — Wide Dome
description: Chunky-knit beanie in charcoal and rust stripe, with an unusually wide dome and reinforced crown seam — designed to sit comfortably around horn-type geneware without stretching out of shape. Rolled cuff can be double-rolled for smaller heads. A Circuit winter staple that also sells well to Tier 3 geneware communities.
functionality: Wide dome accommodates horn-base geneware; retains heat in sub-zero lake-effect conditions.
what_it_says: You've got horns and you're not going to let winter be someone else's problem.
story_hooks: Splitseam Basics is the only Circuit label that specifically markets to geneware wearers — their rise has made bigger brands nervous.
A Circuit bar has a tradition: if you're new and cold, someone will give you a beanie. The color tells you which crew vouched for you.

physical_description.visual_profile: A generously proportioned beanie with an exaggerated crown dome, sitting high and rounded on the head. The wide silhouette reads as deliberately spacious rather than slouchy—it's engineered accommodation masquerading as casual streetwear. Charcoal and rust horizontal stripes run the full length, creating visual rhythm from cuff to peak.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the sides with intentional volume at the crown. The rolled cuff sits flush against the neck without constriction. Designed to accommodate horn-type geneware protrusions (cranial, temporal, or occipital augmentation) without deformation. Smaller heads can double-roll the cuff for a tighter fit.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavy-duty acrylic-blend synthetic knit with reinforced structural fibers woven into the crown seam area. Durable enough for street wear, warm enough for GLMZ winters.
physical_description.texture: Chunky, slightly loose weave with visible horizontal ribbing. The reinforced crown seam creates a subtle ridge line running front to back. Surface has a soft hand despite industrial durability.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray base with rust-orange horizontal stripes spaced roughly 1 inch apart. No additional accent colors; the dual-tone creates enough visual interest.
physical_description.closures: None—pull-on design. The rolled cuff provides gentle tension.
distinctive_features: Unusually wide dome architecture—30–40% larger crown volume than standard beanies
Reinforced crown seam running vertex to occipital area for geneware clearance without stretching
Splitseam Basics woven label at interior cuff (subtle, no logos visible from outside)
Slight color fading typical after 2–3 seasons of street wear
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional. Affordable, durable, designed for working-class bodies with augmentations. Not luxury, not salvage—honest gear.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by Circuit district residents, geneware communities (especially horn-type augmented individuals), and anyone prioritizing practicality over status. Signals self-awareness, embodied modification acceptance, and street-level survival pragmatism. A badge of the GLMZ undercity.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in but maintained. Slight pilling on the crown from friction against cranial implants or horn bases. Cuff may show fading from repeated rolling/unrolling. No patches—it's sturdy enough to last years.

image_prompt: Close-up fashion shot of a charcoal-and-rust striped chunky knit beanie on a dark-skinned model with visible cranial horn geneware (chrome or bone-white texture protruding from temple/crown area). The beanie sits high and spacious, cradling the augmentation naturally. Moody Circuit district alley backdrop—wet neon-reflection pavement, flickering holographic signage. Soft rim light catching the knit texture. Model's expression is neutral, street-smart. Shot from 3/4 angle to show profile and dome volume. --ar 2:3 --v 6
